0.caption: Youngest member of the 1953 Everest expedition; two years later, first up Kangchenjunga with Joe Brown.

1.caption: Two 8000er first ascents — Nanga Parbat solo, then Broad Peak. He died on Chogolisa three weeks after the second.

3.died_note: rockfall while climbing the Crête des Bergers, Dévoluy
3.caption: Aeronautical engineer, Annapurna teammate, first up Makalu — killed at 35 by a single falling stone.

4.caption: The only living member of the two-first-ascents club: Broad Peak 1957, Dhaulagiri 1960.

5.caption: Geologist on the 1953 K2 expedition; the storm-bound attempt to lower him became mountaineering's most famous retreat.

6.caption: Sirdar of the Makalu and Manaslu expeditions and the first person to climb two 8000ers — a distinction usually misremembered as Buhl's.

10.died_note: vanished high on Everest (8 or 9 June)
10.caption: Twenty-two, the youngest of the 1924 party, chosen by Mallory for the final attempt. Part of his remains surfaced in 2024.

12.died_note: hidden crevasse, skiing the Vallée Blanche above Chamonix

13.died_note: vanished high on Everest (8 or 9 June)
13.caption: Lost high on Everest's northeast ridge in 1924, twenty-nine years before the mountain was climbed. "Because it's there."

14.caption: Led the 1932 and 1934 German Nanga Parbat expeditions; the second killed him and nine others.

16.caption: The great Victorian alpinist; the first person to attempt any 8000er, and the first to die on one.

17.born_note: the birthday he adopted after Everest — only 'late May 1914' is recorded

18.caption: Nearly summited K2 with Wiessner in 1939; on top of Cho Oyu fifteen years later.

20.caption: Held six falling men on one ice axe during the K2 retreat — 'The Belay' — then made the first ascent of Gasherbrum I.

21.died_note: roped fall while climbing in the Vercors
21.caption: Annapurna support, Makalu summiter, author of 'Conquistadors of the Useless' — killed on a weekend climb in the Vercors.

23.caption: Deputy leader on Everest 1960, expedition leader on Shishapangma 1964.

24.what: Albert Mummery dies on Nanga Parbat
24.caption: Mummery and Gurkhas Ragobir Thapa and Goman Singh vanish reconnoitering the Rakhiot face — the first deaths on any 8000er.

25.caption: Mallory, Somervell, Norton and Morshead reach ~8225 m without oxygen — higher than any human before them.

26.what: George Mallory and Andrew Irvine dies on Everest
26.caption: Last seen 'going strong for the top' on 8 June (or the 9th — the record allows either). Mallory was found in 1999; part of Irvine in 2024.

27.what: Willy Merkl dies on Nanga Parbat
27.caption: The 1934 disaster: trapped by storm high on the mountain, Merkl, Willo Welzenbach and six Sherpas died slowly over days (Merkl mid-July; conventionally the 16th). His body was found in 1938.

28.what: Maurice Herzog, Louis Lachenal, Lionel Terray, Jean Couzy: attempt on Dhaulagiri
28.caption: At Tukucha the French give up on Dhaulagiri as hopeless and turn to Annapurna — three weeks later they are on top of it.

29.what: Edmund Hillary: attempt on Cho Oyu
29.caption: Shipton's party turns back around 6800 m (early May; the exact day went unrecorded). Hillary's consolation comes a year later.

30.caption: Tenzing and Raymond Lambert, with the Swiss, reach ~8595 m — the highest anyone had ever climbed. He returns the next spring.

31.caption: The American K2 retreat: Schoening's one-axe belay holds six falling men; Art Gilkey, storm-bound with thrombophlebitis, is swept away — or cut himself loose to save the others.

32.caption: Sirdar Gyalzen Norbu summits with Guido Magnone the day after the first ascent — with Manaslu the next year, that made him the first person to climb two 8000ers.

33.caption: Three weeks after Broad Peak, an unauthorized alpine-style side trip: descending unroped in a storm, Buhl steps through a cornice on the southeast ridge. Diemberger, just ahead, finds the breach in the snow.

34.caption: Deputy leader Xu Jing exhausts himself around 8500 m on the north ridge and gives up his place; Wang Fuzhou, Gonpo and Qu Yinhua summit the next morning at 04:20.

50.caption: The birthday Tenzing adopted after Everest — only 'late May 1914' was ever recorded.

60.caption: George Band, the expedition's youngest, worked the icefall route and made no summit bid — his summit came two years later on Kangchenjunga.
